Hi Jamie — thanks for the clear question. Looping in Karthik (security) and Marissa (compliance) to confirm and ship the artifacts. Short answer up front: Redwood's SOC2 Type II (report attached) covers our Hosted API and Redwood-managed Dedicated capacity (i.e., reserved GPU pools that we operate in our cloud regions). Private/on-prem deployments where the customer fully controls the infrastructure are outside the scope of Redwood's SOC2 because those environments are under customer control. Dedicated deployments that are "in-customer VPC" require clarification: if Redwood manages the stack and services inside your VPC as a retained offering (we operate the software and infrastructure on your cloud account under a managed-services agreement), we typically consider that a different model and will need to confirm scope on a case-by-case basis — we can often provide a bridge letter with carve-outs or attestations for a transitional period.

What I'm attaching now:
- redwood_soc2_type2_2025.pdf (SOC2 Type II report for period covering 2025)
- redwood_bridge_letter_template.docx (example bridge letter we use for audits)

Please confirm the exact deployment topology (are you looking at Redwood-managed Dedicated inside Stratus's cloud account, or are you planning to run our software fully on-prem?). Once Karthik confirms the technical scope, we can issue a formal bridge letter for the audit period you specified.

Action items:
- Jamie: confirm which Dedicated model you expect (Redwood-managed in our account vs Redwood-managed in Stratus cloud vs fully on-prem).
- Marissa/Karthik: review and prepare formal bridge letter if applicable; estimate turnaround (we typically can turn a signed bridge letter in 3-5 business days once scope is finalized).

Jamie — quick technical clarifications from my side. Definitions we use internally (short):
- Hosted API: Redwood fully manages model serving, networking, and storage in Redwood-controlled cloud accounts — INCLUDED in SOC2.
- Redwood-managed Dedicated: reserved capacity in Redwood's managed clusters (single-tenant GPU pools we operate) — INCLUDED in SOC2.
- Customer VPC Dedicated (Redwood-managed in-customer account): if Redwood operates services inside your cloud account under a managed-services contract, evidence scope depends on the operational boundaries. We can provide a bridge letter that documents which controls we operate vs which are Stratus responsibilities (networking, host provisioning, physical access) — PARTIAL/CASE-BY-CASE.
- Customer-hosted / on-prem: infrastructure and physical controls are customer responsibility — OUT OF SCOPE for Redwood's SOC2.

Evidence we can provide right now (attached or available on request):
- SOC2 Type II report (attached)
- Tenant isolation architecture and network segmentation diagrams (attachment: tenant_isolation_architecture.pdf)
- Sample KMS audit log extracts and description of key management (we redact customer-specific keys)
- Change control and release notes for the runtime used during the audit period

If you're planning to run Dedicated inside Stratus's cloud but have Redwood manage it, please share: 1) the cloud account model (partner-managed vs Stratus-managed), 2) whether Stratus will retain control of IAM and cloud KMS, and 3) the procurement/legal contact for signing the bridge letter or any NDA. Once we have those, Marissa and I will produce a tailored bridge letter and list of evidence items.

Vanessa — FYI I estimate we can prepare a tailored bridge letter and evidence bundle in 3 business days after we get the Stratus topology and legal contact.
